s: Which doctrine gave birth to the Kapalikas?
x:
The Kapalikas were an important Tantric Shaivite sect that emerged from the Pasupata Shaiva tradition, one of the earliest sects of Shaivism. The Kapalikas were devoted to Lord Bhairava, a fierce manifestation of Shiva. They were known for their austere practices, cremationground rituals and symbolic use of skulls (Kapala), from which they derived their name. Their beliefs and practices influenced later Tantric traditions in different parts of India. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

s: In which text of the Kakatiyas can we find the legal principle that "a woman's property inherits perfectly to her daughters and to her daughter's daughter"?
x:
Purushartha Saramu, authored by Sivadevayya, is an important legal and ethical text of the Kakatiya period. One of its remarkable features is its recognition of women's inheritance rights. The text clearly states that a woman's property could legally pass to her daughters and granddaughters, reflecting the comparatively progressive legal outlook that existed under the Kakatiyas. The work provides valuable information regarding social customs, legal principles and judicial practices prevailing in medieval Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Book – Purushartha Saramu
• Author – Sivadevayya
• Importance – Women's Property Rights

s: Which dynasty built the Thousand Pillar Temple?
x:
The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda is one of the finest architectural achievements of the Kakatiya dynasty. It was constructed during the reign of Rudradeva in 1163 CE. The temple is dedicated to Rudreshwara (Shiva), Vishnu and Surya, making it a Trikuta (three-shrine) temple. It is famous for its exquisitely carved pillars, polished stone sculptures and advanced engineering techniques. The temple represents the mature stage of Kakatiya architecture, combining artistic excellence with structural innovation. It remains one of the most important historical monuments of Telangana. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:

• Dynasty – Kakatiyas
• Builder – Rudradeva
• Location – Hanamkonda

s: The main profession of Jayapa who wrote Nritta Ratnavali?
x:
Jayapa Senani, the celebrated author of Nritta Ratnavali, served as Gajasahini (Commander of the Elephant Corps) under the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva. Although he was a military commander, Jayapa possessed exceptional knowledge of dance and music. His Nritta Ratnavali is one of the most authoritative medieval treatises on Indian dance and describes Marga and Desi dance traditions, dance postures, mudras and performance techniques. The famous dance sculptures of the Ramappa Temple closely follow the principles laid down in this work, making it an invaluable source for the study of medieval Indian dance. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Author – Jayapa Senani
• Position – Gajasahini
• Famous Work – Nritta Ratnavali

s: The dance sculptures at Ramappa Temple in Palampet were carved according to the principles of which book of dance science?
o: A treatise on dance in the Marga Saili style
A treatise on dance in the Desi style
x:
The Ramappa Temple at Palampet, built during the Kakatiya period, is one of the finest examples of medieval temple architecture and sculpture in India. It is especially famous for its beautifully carved Madanikas (bracket figures) depicting various dance postures. These sculptures closely follow the principles laid down in Nrittaratnavali, a celebrated treatise on dance written by Jayapa Senani, the commander-in-chief of the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva. Nrittaratnavali is one of the most important medieval works on Indian dance. It describes both Marga (classical) and Desi (regional) dance traditions, dance postures, hand gestures, movements and performance techniques. The Ramappa sculptures are regarded as a visual representation of the dance forms described in this treatise. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Author – Jayapa Senani
• Work – Nrittaratnavali
• Temple – Ramappa Temple, Palampet
• UNESCO World Heritage Site – Ramappa Temple (2021)

s: Who revived the Perini Shiva Tandavam from the dance panels of the Ramappa Temple?
x: Nataraja Ramakrishna revived the Perini Shiva Tandavam using the dance panels of Ramappa Temple.

s: In which year was the Ramappa Temple at Palampet inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Ramappa (built 1213, famous for its Nrittaratnavali-based madanika brackets) became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021. The years 2014, 2017 and 2023 are distractors.

s: With which name is the Kakatiya painting that led on to the Lepakshi style associated?
x: Kakatiya painting associated with Machaladevi led on to the Lepakshi style.

s: Under which Kakatiya ruler was Jayapa Senani, author of Nrittaratnavali, a commander?
x: Jayapa Senani was Ganapatideva's commander; his Nrittaratnavali covers both marga and desi dance.

s: Which dance treatise is followed by the madanika bracket figures of the Ramappa temple?
x: The Ramappa madanikas follow Jayapa Senani's Nritta Ratnavali, not the Natya Shastra.

s: In which year was the Ramappa Temple built?
x: Ramappa dates to 1213; the Thousand Pillar Temple is of 1163 and the Siddhavatam inscription of 1233.
